scenes.say: Try to tickle yourself right now. It doesn't work.
A part at the back called the cerebellum predicts the feeling of every move you make.
scenes.heading: MEET THE

scenes.say: So when you tickle yourself, it already knows what's coming, and turns the feeling down.
scenes.heading: SELF-TICKLE

scenes.say: When someone else does it, your brain can't predict it. That's why it tickles.
scenes.heading: SOMEONE ELSE

scenes.say: So scientists built a robot that delayed your own tickle by a fraction of a second.
scenes.label: a fraction of a second

scenes.say: And suddenly, it tickled. The longer the delay, the more it tickled.
scenes.heading: THE RESULT
